readout_other: Forelimb EMG amplitude and response latency
direction_notes: TUS induced synchronised forelimb EMG responses from motor cortex; amplitude fell with lower sound pressure and latency rose with deeper anaesthesia. TMAS (TUS plus static magnetic field) gave larger EMG and shorter latency.

exposures.label: TUS (and TMAS with static magnet) of mouse motor cortex

timing.protocol_description: 500 kHz tone bursts of TBD 0.6 ms (300 cycles) at PRF 1 kHz, NTB = 400 pulses per group repeated with period T = 4 s; each train lasted 40 s (10 EMGs collected), three trains per block with 1 min interval. The TMAS arm adds a 0.3 T surface static magnet.

source_quotes.n_subjects: A total of 16 male C57BL/6J (21 ± 2.50 g, 7–8 weeks old) mice were randomly divided into two groups for TUS and TMAS by random number table.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: By referring to the relevant reference which could induce EMG signals (Tufail et al., 2010, 2011; Kubanek, 2018), and considering the safety and effectiveness of ultrasonic intensity, the ultrasonic parameters used in this experiment were as follows: f = 500 kHz, TBD = 0.6 ms, PRF = 1 kHz, NTB = 400, and period T = 4 s, as shown in Figure 2.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: By referring to the relevant reference which could induce EMG signals (Tufail et al., 2010, 2011; Kubanek, 2018), and considering the safety and effectiveness of ultrasonic intensity, the ultrasonic parameters used in this experiment were as follows: f = 500 kHz, TBD = 0.6 ms, PRF = 1 kHz, NTB = 400, and period T = 4 s, as shown in Figure 2.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: By referring to the relevant reference which could induce EMG signals (Tufail et al., 2010, 2011; Kubanek, 2018), and considering the safety and effectiveness of ultrasonic intensity, the ultrasonic parameters used in this experiment were as follows: f = 500 kHz, TBD = 0.6 ms, PRF = 1 kHz, NTB = 400, and period T = 4 s, as shown in Figure 2.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.pressure: Using the above ultrasonic parameters (f = 500 kHz, TBD = 0.6 ms, PRF = 1 kHz, NTB = 400, T = 4 s), the ultrasonic amplitudes were set to 3 V, 1 V, and 0.5 V, corresponding to Psptp of 83 KPa, 38 KPa, and 21 KPa, respectively.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: The ultrasonic transducer (V301, Olympus, Japan, planar ultrasonic transducer, center frequency 500 kHz) was collimated by a sound collimator (self-made, focal length, 2 mm) and fixed on a stereotactic frame and, by moving along three axes (accuracy 0.01 mm), located the target stimulation area of the mouse.

source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: Our study indicated that TMAS could enhance the neuromodulation effect of TUS under conditions of low ultrasound intensity $( \mathrm { M I } \ = \ 0 . 1 2 , \ \mathrm { I s p t a } \ = \ 2 8 8 . 9 \ \mathrm { \ m W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } )$ which meant that TMAS could modulate neural activity more effective and safe.

flags.reason: Psptp measured with a hydrophone 'at the stimulation target (head of the mouse)'; domain (water versus through skull) not clearly stated. Values are for 3 V, 1 V and 0.5 V drive.
Each 'train' lasts 40 s but consists of 400-pulse groups repeated every 4 s, so not one uninterrupted burst.
Study compares TUS with TMAS (TUS plus static magnet); both arms use the same ultrasound exposure, recorded as one exposure.
No sham arm; comparison is TUS versus TMAS.
